subject: Private Deployment: VPC handoff & on-prem packaging — next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@lavidconsortium.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@lavidconsortium.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private Deployment: VPC handoff & on-prem packaging — next steps

Hi Alejandra / Samir —

Thanks again for the call today. This thread will be our operational handoff for the private deployment (VPC peering + private endpoints + on-prem package) so we have a single source for decisions and schedule. Attaching a rough VPC map and an initial mutual action plan for visibility.

Top-level asks from Redwood to confirm by Sept 3: 
- Desired peering model: AWS Transit Gateway vs. VPC peering (we sketched both in the attachment).
- Egress IP ranges you want allowed for outbound calls from the on-prem appliance (if any).
- Preferred maintenance window for initial appliance install (we recommend a 4-hour window during off-peak hours).

I'll schedule a 30-min networking deep-dive with your infra team for Wed (Sep 3). Irene will own port/ACL validation; Marissa will lead the on-prem packaging checklist and shipping. Naomi will coordinate credentials and access (KMS/HSM callouts).

Attachments: lavid-map-vpc-peering-20260901.pdf; mutual-action-plan-Lavid-20260903.xlsx; onprem-package-checklist.txt

Next steps: please confirm the peering choice and availability for Wed.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise GTM - Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@lavidconsortium.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@lavidconsortium.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Deployment: VPC handoff & on-prem packaging — next steps

Ben —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Quick answers:
- We prefer AWS Transit Gateway because we already route multiple accounts through it; simplifies routing and monitoring.
- Egress: we'll allow a short list of fixed outbound IPs. I'll send the list by EOD Tue (Sep 1).
- Maintenance window: Thu Sep 9, 01:00–05:00 PT works for our ops team.

Also looping in a note: we will require the on-prem appliance to support TLS mutual auth and to accept our internal CA certs. Can your onprem package support that out of the box?

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Infra, Lavid Consortium
samir.patel@lavidconsortium.com | +1 212-555-0164

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Deployment: VPC handoff & on-prem packaging — next steps

Samir — great, TGW is noted.

Irene: can you confirm mTLS support in the appliance and what cert formats we accept (PEM, PKCS12)? Also, Marissa will prep an on-prem package variant that includes an option for customer-provided certs.

Alejandra: I attached an updated mutual action plan with milestones that reflect your maintenance window and TGW choice. Please review the milestone owner column.

Irene — action: list of required ingress ports and whether the installer needs to open ephemeral ports for KV/cache synchronization. Deliverable due: 2026-09-03 17:00 PT.
Marissa — action: produce onprem-package checklist entry for mTLS and cert installation steps. Deliverable: 2026-09-04.
Naomi — please prepare a short runbook for KMS-HSM key imports and share the DocuSign access form we need from Lavid.

Thanks all — once we have Irene's port list and Samir's egress IP list we'll book the deep-dive for Sep 3.

Regards,
Ben

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@lavidconsortium.com>, Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@lavidconsortium.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T16:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Deployment: VPC handoff & on-prem packaging — next steps

All —

I ran a quick validation against our appliance and the install flow. Summary of port/egress needs (for TGW model):
- Ingress (from Lavid VPC to appliance VPC): TCP 443 (mTLS API endpoint), TCP 8443 (admin UI), UDP 123 (NTP)
- Outbound (from appliance to Redwood hosted services): TCP 443 to list of Redwood egress IPs (we'll need Samir's confirmed list to finalize ACLs)
- KV/cache sync: TCP 7000–7010 (ephemeral between appliance nodes) — these are internal only and can be over the peered path; no public exposure.

Certs: appliance supports PEM and PKCS12; mTLS with customer CA is supported and we can load CA bundles at install time. Installer script expects: 
- server_cert.pem, server_key.pem (PKCS8 ok), ca_bundle.pem
- optional: pkcs12.pfx if you prefer a single file (installer will extract).

I will drop a minimal onprem-package checklist (text) into the thread and attach the port matrix. Deliverable attached: onprem-package-checklist.txt

Next: Samir, can you confirm the Redwood egress IP allowlist and provide the CA bundle you want us to install (or confirm you'll hand off at install time)?

Thanks,
Irene
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com

From: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@lavidconsortium.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Deployment: VPC handoff & on-prem packaging — next steps

Hi team —

Thanks for the level of detail. Confirmations: 
- We will proceed with AWS Transit Gateway.
- Egress allowlist attached (lavid-egress-allowlist-20260907.csv).
- We will provide CA bundle at install time and prefer the PKCS12 option for our internal toolchain.
- Install window confirmed: Thu Sep 9, 01:00–05:00 PT.

A couple notes for the runbook: our operations team requires a rollback procedure in case the appliance impacts internal routing. Please include a short rollback checklist (stop/remove appliance, detach TGW route table changes, validate connectivity). If you can add that to the runbook Naomi prepares, that would be ideal.

Looking forward to the deep-dive on Sep 3.

Best,
Alejandra
Head of IT Security — Lavid Consortium
alejandra.ruiz@lavidconsortium.com
